sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐形。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: If you drive from Oakland to Los Angeles in February, you'll pass through a spectacular scene.
sentences.zh: 如果你在二月从奥克兰开车去洛杉矶，你会路过一处壮丽的景色。

sentences.en: Neat, symmetrical rows of trees covered with pink and white flowers stretching on for hundreds of
sentences.zh: 整齐、对称的树行上开满了粉色和白色的花朵，绵延数

sentences.en: miles.
sentences.zh: 百英里。

sentences.en: This is the annual California almond bloom, and it really is massive.
sentences.zh: 这是一年一度的加州杏花盛开期，场面确实十分壮观。

sentences.en: California almond trees
sentences.zh: 加州杏树

sentences.en: take up a million acres of land in the Central Valley.
sentences.zh: 在中央谷地占据了一百万英亩的土地。

sentences.en: When the petals fall off, they carpet the
sentences.zh: 当花瓣落下时，它们给

sentences.en: road and create this sweet smell.
sentences.zh: 道路铺上了一层地毯，并散发出这种甜美的气味。

sentences.en: And the almond bloom also has its own distinctive sound.
sentences.zh: 而且杏花盛开时也有其独特的声音。

sentences.en: You can
sentences.zh: 你甚至

sentences.en: actually hear it before you even walk into the orchard.
sentences.zh: 还没走进果园就能听到。

sentences.en: That's the sound of thousands of bees from
sentences.zh: 那是来自加利福尼亚州莫德斯托

sentences.en: an orchard outside of Modesto, California.
sentences.zh: 市外果园里成千上万只蜜蜂的声音。

sentences.en: To create a single almond, a blossom needs as many as a dozen
sentences.zh: 为了孕育一颗杏子，一朵花需要经历多达十几

sentences.en: bee visits.
sentences.zh: 次蜜蜂造访。

sentences.en: That means you need roughly 80,000 bees to pollinate an acre of almonds.
sentences.zh: 这意味着你需要大约8万只蜜蜂来为一英亩的杏树授粉。

sentences.en: That's Adam Ellington.
sentences.zh: 那是亚当·埃灵顿。

sentences.en: He's a reporter covering the environment for Bloomberg.
sentences.zh: 他是彭博社的一名环境记者。

sentences.en: He also hosts the
sentences.zh: 他还主持了播客

sentences.en: podcast, The Business of Bees.
sentences.zh: 《蜜蜂生意》。

sentences.en: When you think of bees in business, you're probably thinking of honey.
sentences.zh: 当你想起与商业有关的蜜蜂时，你可能首先会想到蜂蜜。

sentences.en: But in fact, honey has little to
sentences.zh: 但事实上，蜂蜜与如今的

sentences.en: do with commercial beekeeping today.
sentences.zh: 商业养蜂关系不大。

sentences.en: Every winter, beekeepers from every corner of the United States
sentences.zh: 每年冬天，来自美国各个角落的

sentences.en: descend on California to pollinate almonds.
sentences.zh: 养蜂人都会涌向加利福尼亚为杏树授粉。

sentences.en: Almonds have a window of about two weeks for
sentences.zh: 杏树授粉的

sentences.en: pollination to occur.
sentences.zh: 时间窗口大约只有两周。

sentences.en: Otherwise, the blossoms won't turn into fruit.
sentences.zh: 否则，花朵就无法变成果实。

sentences.en: The demand is so high,
sentences.zh: 需求量如此之大，

sentences.en: it takes almost every beehive in the country to do the job.
sentences.zh: 几乎需要全国所有的蜂箱来完成这项工作。

sentences.en: Upwards of two million hives.
sentences.zh: 超过两百万个蜂箱。

sentences.en: This is the largest managed pollination event on Earth.
sentences.zh: 这是地球上规模最大的受人工管理的授粉活动。

sentences.en: This is John Miller.
sentences.zh: 这是约翰·米勒。

sentences.en: He's a fourth-generation beekeeper from North Dakota.
sentences.zh: 他是来自北达科他州的第四代养蜂人。

sentences.en: And every year,
sentences.zh: 每年，

sentences.en: John brings 13,000 hives over 1,500 miles to the Central Valley.
sentences.zh: 约翰都会带着1.3万个蜂箱跨越1500多英里来到中央谷地。

sentences.en: I've got the best job on Earth.
sentences.zh: 我有世界上最棒的工作。

sentences.en: Look at this.
sentences.zh: 看这个。

sentences.en: It's a beautiful spring day in Northern California.
sentences.zh: 这是北加州一个美丽的春日。

sentences.en: Almond trees are in bloom.
sentences.zh: 杏树正在盛开。

sentences.en: I just love it.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢了。

sentences.en: What are we looking at right here?
sentences.zh: 我们现在看到的是什么？

sentences.en: This is the top of the hive.
sentences.zh: 这是蜂箱的顶部。

sentences.en: These are the occupants.
sentences.zh: 这些是里面的居民。

sentences.en: These are the little bees.
sentences.zh: 这些是小蜜蜂。

sentences.en: They're hanging out.
sentences.zh: 它们在闲逛。

sentences.en: There's a...
there's...
well, this guy just landed.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这家伙刚落下来。

sentences.en: For a beekeeper like John, pollination isn't just big business.
sentences.zh: 对于像约翰这样的养蜂人来说，授粉不仅仅是大生意。

sentences.en: It's most of his business.
sentences.zh: 这是他大部分的业务。

sentences.en: In recent
sentences.zh: 在过去

sentences.en: years, almond pollination has become so lucrative, it accounts for about two-thirds of John's income.
sentences.zh: 几年里，杏树授粉变得如此赚钱，以至于占了约翰收入的大约三分之二。

sentences.en: How much of this honey actually will go to making honey for people to eat?
sentences.zh: 这些蜂蜜实际上有多少会用来制作供人食用的蜂蜜？

sentences.en: None.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: Instead of selling the honey, John says it's more cost-effective to just leave it in the hive as
sentences.zh: 约翰说，与其出售蜂蜜，不如把它留在蜂箱里作为

sentences.en: food for the bees.
sentences.zh: 蜜蜂的食物更划算。

sentences.en: After pollinating almonds, John will load his bees onto a semi-truck,
sentences.zh: 在为杏树授粉后，约翰会把蜜蜂装上卡车，

sentences.en: and they'll move from one crop to another in other states.
sentences.zh: 它们将在其他州从一种作物转移到另一种作物。

sentences.en: You know, they'll go from almonds to plums to cherries to apples to vine crops to pit fruits
sentences.zh: 你知道的，它们会从杏子转到李子、樱桃、苹果、藤本作物、核果、

sentences.en: to cotton to lima beans to watermelons, and then their season is over.
sentences.zh: 棉花、利马豆到西瓜，然后它们的季节就结束了。

sentences.en: Farmers have known for centuries that putting a hive of honeybees in an orchard results in
sentences.zh: 几个世纪以来，农民们一直都知道，在果园里放一个蜜蜂箱

sentences.en: more blossoms becoming cherries, almonds, or apples.
sentences.zh: 可以使更多的花朵变成樱桃、杏子或苹果。

sentences.en: But it's only in the last 30 years that
sentences.zh: 但直到最近30年，

sentences.en: pollination services like the kind that John provides have become such an enormous part of
sentences.zh: 像约翰所提供的这种授粉服务才成为美国农业中如此巨大的一

sentences.en: American agriculture.
sentences.zh: 部分。

sentences.en: Today, bees have become more livestock than wild creatures.
sentences.zh: 如今，蜜蜂已经变得更像是牲畜而不是野生生物。

sentences.en: Basically,
sentences.zh: 基本上，

sentences.en: tiny little winged cows that depend on humans for shelter, food, and even medicine.
sentences.zh: 它们就是长着翅膀的微型奶牛，依靠人类提供庇护、食物甚至是药物。

sentences.en: But for thousands of years, our relationship with bees was much simpler.
sentences.zh: 但在数千年里，我们与蜜蜂的关系要简单得多。

sentences.en: It was really all about the
sentences.zh: 这完全是为了

sentences.en: honey.
sentences.zh: 蜂蜜。

sentences.en: Way before sugar came along, honey was one of the few sweeteners we had.
sentences.zh: 早在糖出现之前，蜂蜜就是我们仅有的几种甜味剂之一。

sentences.en: There are 8,000-year-old cave paintings in Spain of people collecting wild honey.
sentences.zh: 西班牙有8000年历史的岩画描绘了人们收集野生蜂蜜的场景。

sentences.en: And once humans got a taste for honey, they'd do almost anything to get it.
sentences.zh: 一旦人类尝到了蜂蜜的甜头，他们就会不惜一切代价得到它。

sentences.en: Alexander Zomchek is an apiculturist at the University of Miami, Ohio.
sentences.zh: 亚历山大·佐姆切克是俄亥俄州迈阿密大学的养蜂专家。

sentences.en: He studies bees and agriculture.
sentences.zh: 他研究蜜蜂和农业。

sentences.en: To put it gently, we found ourselves as plunderers when we tripped across natural beehives,
sentences.zh: 委婉地说，当我们偶然发现天然蜂巢时，我们就像是一群掠夺者，

sentences.en: the Winnie the Pooh trees in the wild.
sentences.zh: 也就是现实生活中的小熊维尼树。

sentences.en: And when people came across one of these trees,
sentences.zh: 当人们偶然发现其中一棵这样的树时，

sentences.en: they would cut it down.
sentences.zh: 他们会把它砍倒。

sentences.en: And in so doing, rob the bees of this honey.
sentences.zh: 并以此剥夺蜜蜂的蜂蜜。

sentences.en: It was not a wonderful
sentences.zh: 这可不是一段美好的

sentences.en: experience.
sentences.zh: 经历。

sentences.en: We didn't have bee suits.
sentences.zh: 我们当时没有防蜂服。

sentences.en: It was a pretty raw event.
sentences.zh: 那是一个相当原始的过程。

sentences.en: These collectors would smother and
sentences.zh: 这些采蜜人会用烟把蜜蜂熏窒息并杀死

sentences.en: kill the bees with smoke, and then they'd take the honey.
sentences.zh: 它们，然后拿走蜂蜜。

sentences.en: It was not exactly a sustainable process.
sentences.zh: 这绝对不是一个可持续的过程。

sentences.en: Slowly over time, it really dawned on us that, well, what if we tried to put them in a container?
sentences.zh: 随着时间推移，我们慢慢意识到，如果我们试着把它们放进容器里会怎么样？

sentences.en: By the Middle Ages, beekeepers in Europe had designed a method of capturing swarms of bees
sentences.zh: 到中世纪时，欧洲的养蜂人已经设计出了一种方法，可以捕捉蜂群

sentences.en: and then putting them inside woven upside-down baskets called skeps.
sentences.zh: 并将它们放入被称为“skep”的倒扣编织篮中。

sentences.en: For all you vexillologists out there, there's actually a bee skep on the state flag of Utah.
sentences.zh: 对于你们所有旗帜学爱好者来说，犹他州州旗上其实就有一个蜂窝篮。

sentences.en: It's got a little door for the bees to come in and out, and it's positioned right in the center
sentences.zh: 它有一个供蜜蜂进出的小门，位置正好在

sentences.en: between the words Utah and industry.
sentences.zh: “犹他”和“工业”这两个词的正中间。

sentences.en: An obvious advantage of the skep design was that you didn't
sentences.zh: 蜂窝篮设计的一个明显优势在于，你不需要

sentences.en: have to go out and hunt for the honey and chop down a tree to get it.
sentences.zh: 出去寻找蜂蜜并砍倒一棵树来获取它。

sentences.en: And the skeps were portable.
sentences.zh: 而且这些蜂窝篮是便携的。

sentences.en: When the first Europeans came to America, they brought along a few skeps full of honeybees,
sentences.zh: 当第一批欧洲人来到美洲时，他们随身带来了一些装满蜜蜂的蜂窝篮，

sentences.en: which are actually not native to North America.
sentences.zh: 而蜜蜂其实并不是北美本土的物种。

sentences.en: The species the Europeans brought over is called Apis mellifera.
sentences.zh: 欧洲人带来的物种叫做西方蜜蜂。

sentences.en: It's Latin for honey carrier.
sentences.zh: 在拉丁语中是“运蜜者”的意思。

sentences.en: Of the 20,000 bee species in the world, Apis mellifera is the only one that can produce enough honey
sentences.zh: 在全世界的2万种蜜蜂中，西方蜜蜂是唯一一种能够生产足够多

sentences.en: to be useful for humans.
sentences.zh: 对人类有用蜂蜜的蜜蜂。

sentences.en: It formed larger colonies.
sentences.zh: 它能形成更大的蜂群。

sentences.en: It had a gentle nature.
sentences.zh: 它性格温和。

sentences.en: It was a good honey producer.
sentences.zh: 它是一个好的蜂蜜生产者。

sentences.en: It was one that we could use around the world, and that was our golden retriever.
sentences.zh: 这是我们可以在世界各地使用的品种，这就是我们的金毛寻回犬。

sentences.en: And these docile, sweet-tempered bees did really well in America.
sentences.zh: 这些温顺、脾气好的蜜蜂在美洲表现得非常好。

sentences.en: There's a good saying by a 17th-century scholar that said the honeybees did better than the settlers did.
sentences.zh: 17世纪的一位学者有一句名言，说蜜蜂比定居者过得还要好。

sentences.en: That's Tammy Horn-Potter.
sentences.zh: 那是塔米·霍恩-波特。

sentences.en: I am the Kentucky State ApiariSt. I work with the Kentucky Department of Agriculture.
sentences.zh: 我是肯塔基州州立养蜂人。我与肯塔基州农业部合作。

sentences.en: Tammy also wrote a book titled Bees in America, How the Honeybee Shaped a Nation.
sentences.zh: 塔米还写了一本书，名为《美洲的蜜蜂：蜜蜂如何塑造一个国家》。

sentences.en: And she says the honeybees loved their new continent.
sentences.zh: 她说蜜蜂非常喜欢它们的新大陆。

sentences.en: There were plenty of stands of a type of a species of tree called black gum.
sentences.zh: 那里有大量一种叫做黑树胶树的树木。

sentences.en: And black gum trees are notable because they decay from the inside out very quickly.
sentences.zh: 黑树胶树引人注目的一点是它们会从内向外非常迅速地腐烂。

sentences.en: They would swarm and take up residence in these trees.
sentences.zh: 蜜蜂会成群结队地在这些树中安家。

sentences.en: And so honeybees did very well.
sentences.zh: 因此蜜蜂过得很好。

sentences.en: So by the middle of the 19th century, honeybees were well-established in North America.
sentences.zh: 所以在19世纪中叶，蜜蜂已经在北美扎根。

sentences.en: People were still keeping them in skeps or hunting small amounts of wild honey in nature.
sentences.zh: 人们仍然把它们养在蜂窝篮里，或者在自然界中寻找少量的野生蜂蜜。

sentences.en: But eventually everything changed with a Presbyterian minister named Lorenzo Langstroth.
sentences.zh: 但最终，这一切随着一位名叫洛伦佐·朗斯特罗特的长老会牧师而改变了。

sentences.en: After attending seminary at Yale, Langstroth returned to his hometown of Philadelphia in 1848.
sentences.zh: 在耶鲁大学神学院就读后，朗斯特罗特于1848年回到了他的家乡费城。

sentences.en: And during this time, Langstroth began to struggle with mental illness.
sentences.zh: 正是在这段时间里，朗斯特罗特开始与精神疾病作斗争。

sentences.en: In diaries from the time, his family referred to it as head troubles.
sentences.zh: 在他当时的日记中，他的家人称之为“头部毛病”。

sentences.en: Today, it's what we'd call seasonal affective disorder.
sentences.zh: 在今天，这就是我们所说的季节性情绪失调。

sentences.en: Back then, a standard prescription to fight depression would be laudanum.
sentences.zh: 而在当时，对抗抑郁症的标准处方是鸦片酊。

sentences.en: That's an alcoholic solution containing morphine.
sentences.zh: 那是一种含有吗啡的酒精溶液。

sentences.en: But Langstroth's doctor wanted to try something more gentle.
sentences.zh: 但朗斯特罗特的医生想尝试一些更温和的方法。

sentences.en: He told him to spend more time outdoors, which he did.
sentences.zh: 他告诉他多花点时间在户外，他也照做了。

sentences.en: He would take long walks on his own out in nature.
sentences.zh: 他会独自在大自然中进行长时间的散步。

sentences.en: And he developed an extreme fascination with wild honeybees.
sentences.zh: 并且他对野生蜜蜂产生了极大的痴迷。

sentences.en: He literally just spent hours and days and weeks and months staring at these hollow bee trees until an idea finally clicked in his mind.
sentences.zh: 他 literalmente 真的花了几个小时、几天、几周和几个月的时间盯着这些中空的蜂树，直到一个想法最终在他的脑海中豁然开朗。

sentences.en: Langstroth noticed something about beehives in the wild.
sentences.zh: 朗斯特罗特注意到了野生蜂箱的一些特点。

sentences.en: There was this pattern, a kind of mathematical precision to the spacing between the honeycombs.
sentences.zh: 这里有一种规律，蜂巢之间的间距具有某种数学般的精确性。

sentences.en: And the moment came when he realized there is this same, same exact space, a carpenter's number, three-eighths of an inch, between every one of these combs.
sentences.zh: 而那个时刻到来了，他意识到在每一个蜂巢之间，都有着这样一个完全相同、精确的木匠数字——八分之三英寸的间距。

sentences.en: And they were measured again and again, different hives, different times, different colonies.
sentences.zh: 而且它们在不同的蜂箱、不同的时间和不同的蜂群中被一次又一次地测量。

sentences.en: And it's always three-eighths of an inch.
sentences.zh: 并且它总是八分之三英寸。

sentences.en: Langstroth called this area the bee space.
sentences.zh: 朗斯特罗特把这个区域称为“蜂路”。

sentences.en: Three-eighths of an inch is the exact amount of space bees need to move around a colony.
sentences.zh: 八分之三英寸正是蜜蜂在蜂群周围移动所需的精确空间大小。

sentences.en: They're like little hallways between the honeycombs.
sentences.zh: 它们就像是蜂巢之间的小走廊。

sentences.en: So then, Langstroth took this idea of the bee space and he put it in a box.
sentences.zh: 于是，朗斯特罗特将这个关于蜂路的想法放进了一个箱子里。

sentences.en: Inside each wooden hive box, he would hang a series of removable frames, kind of like empty picture frames.
sentences.zh: 在每个木制蜂箱内部，他会悬挂一系列可拆卸的框架，有点像空的相框。

sentences.en: And each one was spaced three-eighths of an inch apart.
sentences.zh: 并且每一个框架的间距都是八分之三英寸。

sentences.en: When Langstroth put bees inside the box, they looked up at the frames and they thought,
sentences.zh: 当朗斯特罗特把蜜蜂放进箱子里时，它们抬头看着这些框架，心想，

sentences.en: Hey, you know what?
sentences.zh: 嘿，你知道吗？

sentences.en: This looks a lot like home.
sentences.zh: 这看起来太像家了。

sentences.en: Then other bees joined in, and before you know it, they were making colonies inside these boxes.
sentences.zh: 然后其他蜜蜂也加入了进来，不知不觉中，它们就在这些箱子里建造了蜂群。

sentences.en: And the Langstroth hive was invented.
sentences.zh: 于是朗斯特罗特蜂箱就被发明出来了。

sentences.en: It's the modern beehive, the one that we still have today.
sentences.zh: 这就是现代蜂箱，也就是我们今天仍在使用的那种。

sentences.en: It was the first artificial hive which could be easily controlled and moved around.
sentences.zh: 它是第一个可以轻松控制和移动的人工蜂箱。

sentences.en: It changed everything about beekeeping.
sentences.zh: 它彻底改变了养蜂业。

sentences.en: Oh, it was fundamental.
sentences.zh: 哦，这太关键了。

sentences.en: I mean, there's just no doubt about that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是毫无疑问的。

sentences.en: Because once beekeepers can manage colonies, they can check on their health.
sentences.zh: 因为一旦养蜂人能够管理蜂群，他们就能检查它们的健康状况。

sentences.en: Say if it's a drought.
sentences.zh: 比如说遇到干旱。

sentences.en: They can help provide supplemental food.
sentences.zh: 他们可以协助提供补充饲料。

sentences.en: Langstroth's innovations meant people could keep more bees, and the bees could reuse their honeycombs
sentences.zh: 朗斯特罗的创新意味着人们可以养更多的蜜蜂，而且蜜蜂可以重复使用它们的蜂巢

sentences.en: because people weren't destroying them all the time, which allowed honey production to go way up.
sentences.zh: 因为人们不用一直破坏它们，这使得蜂蜜产量大幅上升。

sentences.en: Langstroth published a book of his findings in 1853 called The Hive and the Honey Bee.
sentences.zh: 朗斯特罗于1853年出版了一本关于他研究成果的书，名为《蜂巢与蜜蜂》。

sentences.en: It's still widely read in beekeeping circles today.
sentences.zh: 直到今天，它在养蜂界依然被广泛阅读。

sentences.en: And once it got out, beekeeping became big business all over the world.
sentences.zh: 一旦消息传开，养蜂业在世界各地都成了大生意。

sentences.en: The hives are crammed with honey and ready for man to rob.
sentences.zh: 蜂箱里塞满了蜂蜜，等待着人类去采收。

sentences.en: The bees have made millions of journeys to add to that precious store.
sentences.zh: 为了给这珍贵的储藏添砖加瓦，蜜蜂已经飞行了数百万次。

sentences.en: To be or not to be.
sentences.zh: 生存还是毁灭。

sentences.en: To be it is.
sentences.zh: 生存就是了。

sentences.en: After World War I, people kept innovating and honey production went from family farming to a giant commercial operation.
sentences.zh: 第一次世界大战后，人们不断创新，蜂蜜产量从家庭农业转变为巨型商业运作。

sentences.en: By the end of World War II, there were something like 5.9 million commercial beehives in the United States.
sentences.zh: 到二战结束时，美国大约有590万个商业蜂箱。

sentences.en: It also set the stage for the next chapter of beekeeping, the rise of commercial pollination.
sentences.zh: 这也为养蜂业的下一个篇章——商业授粉的兴起奠定了基础。

sentences.en: In the 1950s, small family farms started getting pushed out by big companies and industrial agriculture.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪50年代，小型家庭农场开始被大公司和工业化农业挤出局。

sentences.en: While family farms had fields with different crops growing side by side,
sentences.zh: 虽然家庭农场的田地里种植着不同的作物，彼此相邻，

sentences.en: the new model replaced the whole system with ever-expanding fields devoted to growing just one plant.
sentences.zh: 但新的模式用不断扩展的、专门种植单一植物的田地取代了整个系统。

sentences.en: Instead of planting cover crops to replenish the soil after the harvest, they'd just use fertilizer.
sentences.zh: 他们不再在收获后种植覆盖作物来补充土壤，而是直接使用化肥。

sentences.en: Some of our commercial crops, like corn, rice, and wheat, are pollinated by the wind.
sentences.zh: 我们的一些经济作物，如玉米、水稻和小麦，是通过风力授粉的。

sentences.en: But many of our fruits and vegetables rely on insects to do the job.
sentences.zh: 但我们的许多水果和蔬菜依靠昆虫来完成这项工作。

sentences.en: As the entire business became more and more industrialized and shifted to monoculture,
sentences.zh: 随着整个行业越来越工业化并转向单一作物种植，

sentences.en: there was a need for greater certainty when it came to pollination.
sentences.zh: 在授粉方面需要更高的确定性。

sentences.en: Commercial bees, thanks to the Langstroth hive, were a perfect fit.
sentences.zh: 多亏了朗斯特罗蜂箱，商业蜜蜂堪称绝配。

sentences.en: Controlled by humans and highly portable, they were able to do more pollinating in a day than most wild insects do in a week.
sentences.zh: 它们由人类控制且极易搬运，一天内能完成的授粉工作比大多数野生昆虫一周内做的还要多。

sentences.en: So instead of trusting the local ecosystem to pollinate their crops,
sentences.zh: 因此，许多农场不再依赖当地的生态系统为农作物授粉，

sentences.en: many farms came to depend on this single domesticated species of bee.
sentences.zh: 而是开始依赖这种单一的驯化蜜蜂。

sentences.en: As farmers grew more crops, commercial beekeepers started earning more money by renting out their bees as pollinators.
sentences.zh: 随着农场种植更多的作物，商业养蜂人开始通过出租他们的蜜蜂作为授粉媒介来赚取更多的钱。

sentences.en: But while pollination is big business in the United States,
sentences.zh: 但虽然授粉在美国是大生意，

sentences.en: actually, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 实际上，美国

sentences.en: is pretty much the only country that does this.
sentences.zh: 几乎是唯一这样一个做的国家。

sentences.en: Jeff Lee is a commercial beekeeper from North Carolina.
sentences.zh: 杰夫·李是来自北卡罗来纳州的一名商业养蜂人。

sentences.en: Every year, he ships 1,200 hives to California to pollinate almonds.
sentences.zh: 每年，他都会向加利福尼亚州运送1200个蜂箱来为杏树授粉。

sentences.en: In March, they'll come back to North Carolina, where I will do highbush blueberry pollination.
sentences.zh: 三月份，它们会回到北卡罗来纳州，我将在那里进行高丛蓝莓授粉。

sentences.en: After that, they will go up to Maine.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，它们将前往缅因州。

sentences.en: That's where they'll do the lowbush blueberry pollination.
sentences.zh: 那里的工作是进行低丛蓝莓授粉。

sentences.en: And some will go to Wisconsin for cranberry pollination.
sentences.zh: 有些会去威斯康星州进行蔓越莓授粉。

sentences.en: And others will come right back to North Carolina for a cucumber and watermelon pollination.
sentences.zh: 还有一些会直接回到北卡罗来纳州进行黄瓜和西瓜授粉。

sentences.en: Today, commercial beekeepers get most of their income from pollination.
sentences.zh: 如今，商业养蜂人的大部分收入来自授粉。

sentences.en: They're paid around $200 per hive for a few weeks of pollinating almonds.
sentences.zh: 在为杏树授粉的几周里，每个蜂箱大约能获得200美元的报酬。

sentences.en: So if you do the math, $200 per hive times, say, 1,000 hives, that's $200,000.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你算一下，每个蜂箱200美元乘以比方说1000个蜂箱，那就是20万美元。

sentences.en: Which sounds like pretty good money for three weeks of work.
sentences.zh: 对于三周的工作来说，这听起来是一笔相当不错的收入。

sentences.en: But Lee says the cost for keeping bees alive has shot through the roof in the last couple years.
sentences.zh: 但李说，在过去的几年里，保持蜜蜂存活的成本已经急剧飙升。

sentences.en: Right now, beekeepers are facing one big challenge.
sentences.zh: 目前，养蜂人正面临一个巨大的挑战。

sentences.en: You might already know about it if you watch the worst movie of 2008,
sentences.zh: 如果你看过2008年最烂的那部电影，你可能已经知道了，

sentences.en: The Happening, starring Mark Wahlberg as a beleaguered science teacher.
sentences.zh: 《灭顶之灾》，由马克·沃尔伯格主演，饰演一名饱受困扰的科学老师。

sentences.en: I don't know if any of you guys have heard about this article in the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你们当中是否有人听说过《纽约时报》上的这篇文章。

sentences.en: Well, apparently, honeybees are just disappearing all over the country.
sentences.zh: 好吧，显然，全国各地的蜜蜂正在成群消失。

sentences.en: Tens of millions of them.
sentences.zh: 数以千万计。

sentences.en: All right, let's hear some theories about why this might be happening.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们听听关于为什么会发生这种事的一些理论。

sentences.en: Nobody?
sentences.zh: 没有人吗？

sentences.en: You're not interested in what happened to the bees?
sentences.zh: 你们对蜜蜂发生了什么不感兴趣吗？

sentences.en: Tragically, I have seen The Happening.
sentences.zh: 悲剧的是，我看过《灭顶之灾》。

sentences.en: Marky Mark is not good in this movie.
sentences.zh: 马克·马克在这部电影里表现并不好。

sentences.en: But he's right.
sentences.zh: 但他是对的。

sentences.en: The bees are dying.
sentences.zh: 蜜蜂正在死去。

sentences.en: Adult bees leave the hive and never come back, leaving the babies to die.
sentences.zh: 成年蜜蜂离开蜂巢后就再也没有回来，留下幼蜂死去。

sentences.en: Researchers blame pesticides, disease, and parasites.
sentences.zh: 研究人员将其归咎于杀虫剂、疾病和寄生虫。

sentences.en: Back in 2007, reports of a mysterious bee plague called Colony Collapse Disorder were making headlines all over the country.
sentences.zh: 早在2007年，被称为“蜂群崩溃综合征”的神秘蜜蜂瘟疫的报道登上了全国各地的头条。

sentences.en: And it got people worried.
sentences.zh: 这让人们感到担忧。

sentences.en: There were articles warning us about the end of bees.
sentences.zh: 有文章警告我们蜜蜂的末日。

sentences.en: There were studies by freaked-out scientists.
sentences.zh: 有吓坏了的科学家进行的研究。

sentences.en: Colony Collapse is when all the bees in a colony just disappear in the course of a few days.
sentences.zh: 蜂群崩溃是指蜂群中的所有蜜蜂在几天内突然消失。

sentences.en: There's no bee corpses to do an autopsy on and no obvious signs of poisoning.
sentences.zh: 没有蜂尸可供尸检，也没有明显的中毒迹象。

sentences.en: Around 2007, it was happening a lot.
sentences.zh: 2007年前后，这种情况经常发生。

sentences.en: The number of cases technically labeled as colony collapse has actually gone down since then.
sentences.zh: 自那以后，被技术上标记为蜂群崩溃的案例数量实际上已经下降了。

sentences.en: But Jeff Lee says it's still happening.
sentences.zh: 但杰夫·李表示，这种情况仍在发生。

sentences.en: Bees disappearing or dying in huge numbers.
sentences.zh: 蜜蜂大批消失或死亡。

sentences.en: A recent survey of commercial beekeepers found the average yearly die-off rate is about 40 percent,
sentences.zh: 最近对商业养蜂人的一项调查发现，平均每年的死亡率约为40%，

sentences.en: which is way higher than the 10 to 15 percent, which used to be normal.
sentences.zh: 这远远高于过去正常的10%到15%。

sentences.en: Researchers point to increased use of pesticides as one factor.
sentences.zh: 研究人员指出，杀虫剂使用量的增加是一个因素。

sentences.en: And when the bees started dying, there were protests.
sentences.zh: 当蜜蜂开始死亡时，抗议活动也随之而来。

sentences.en: Save the bees!
sentences.zh: 拯救蜜蜂！

sentences.en: Give bees a child!
sentences.zh: 给蜜蜂一个孩子！

sentences.en: No more poison!
sentences.zh: 不要再有毒药！

sentences.en: You're not just killing the bees, you're killing yourself!
sentences.zh: 你们不只是在杀死蜜蜂，你们是在杀死自己！

sentences.en: But pesticides aren't the only culprit.
sentences.zh: 但杀虫剂并不是唯一的罪魁祸首。

sentences.en: Another problem is an invasive parasitic mite from Asia called Varroa destructor.
sentences.zh: 另一个问题是来自亚洲的入侵寄生螨，被称为狄氏瓦螨（大蜂螨）。

sentences.en: Once it has penetrated the beehive, the Varroa mite multiplies in the brood cells where the queen has laid her eggs.
sentences.zh: 一旦进入蜂箱，瓦螨就会在蜂王产卵的育雏房里大量繁殖。

sentences.en: They use their mouthparts to suck a blood-like fluid from the bee larvae and then lay their eggs in the brood cell.
sentences.zh: 它们用口器吸食蜜蜂幼虫体内的血样液体，然后将卵产在育雏房里。

sentences.en: This is a video from 2017.
sentences.zh: 这是一段2017年的视频。

sentences.en: It's made by Bayer, the largest producer of pesticides in the world.
sentences.zh: 它由全球最大的杀虫剂生产商拜耳公司制作。

sentences.en: And given that, of course, Bayer wants us to focus on the mites.
sentences.zh: 鉴于此，拜耳当然希望我们把注意力集中在螨虫上。

sentences.en: By the time the bee hatches, it is weakened, often infected with viruses, and has a shortened lifespan.
sentences.zh: 当蜜蜂孵化出来时，它已经虚弱不堪，通常感染了病毒，并且寿命缩短。

sentences.en: The Varroa mite can also be carried by the bee into other beehives.
sentences.zh: 瓦螨还可以被蜜蜂携带到其他蜂箱中。

sentences.en: Varroa mites have wiped out tens of millions of beehives in the United States.
sentences.zh: 瓦螨已经消灭了美国数以千万计的蜂箱。

sentences.en: Since the European honeybee didn't evolve alongside the mite, the bees don't have a natural defense.
sentences.zh: 由于欧洲蜜蜂没有与这种螨虫共同进化，因此蜜蜂没有天然防御能力。

sentences.en: And because most of the commercial beehives in the country end up in a single place, in California every February,
sentences.zh: 而且由于国内大多数商业蜂箱每年二月最终都会集中在一个地方——加利福尼亚州，

sentences.en: we've created the ideal scenario for Varroa mites to spread from one hive to another.
sentences.zh: 我们为瓦螨从一个蜂箱传播到另一个蜂箱创造了理想的条件。

sentences.en: Which is a real threat to our food supply.
sentences.zh: 这对我们的食物供应构成了真正的威胁。

sentences.en: Because our whole agricultural system has become dependent on this single, vulnerable species of insect.
sentences.zh: 因为我们的整个农业系统已经变得依赖于这种单一、脆弱的昆虫物种。

sentences.en: And now, it's hard to imagine feeding the country without them.
sentences.zh: 现在，很难想象没有它们该如何养活这个国家。

sentences.en: It's inextricable from industrial ag, which the United States excels in.
sentences.zh: 它与美国引以为傲的工业化农业密不可分。

sentences.en: Not just excels, it defines industrial ag.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是擅长，它定义了工业化农业。

sentences.en: You know, that's at the root of all of our ability to have monocultural orchards.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是我们能够拥有单一种植果园的所有能力之根源。

sentences.en: You know, your pumpkins and your raspberries and blueberries and blackberries.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你的南瓜、树莓、蓝莓和黑莓。

sentences.en: You know, you don't get those massive tracts of production without pollination.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果没有授粉，你就无法获得如此大规模的生产。

sentences.en: But there are farmers today who are trying to rely less on honeybee livestock by reintroducing wild bees and insects into the pollination landscape.
sentences.zh: 但今天的许多农民正试图通过将野生蜜蜂和昆虫重新引入授粉景观中，来减少对家养蜜蜂的依赖。

sentences.en: According to entomologists, just a small amount of plant diversity can help boost the population of wild bees and other pollinators like butterflies and beetles.
sentences.zh: 据昆虫学家称，只需少量的植物多样性，就能帮助促进野生蜜蜂以及蝴蝶和甲虫等其他授粉媒介的数量。

sentences.en: An example of this is something called a pollinator hedgerow.
sentences.zh: 这方面的一个例子被称为授粉媒介绿篱。

sentences.en: Basically, a small strip of native weeds or flowers near the edge of a field that can provide habitat and food for wild insects and bees all year round.
sentences.zh: 基本上，这是田地边缘的一小片原生杂草或野花，可以全年为野生昆虫和蜜蜂提供栖息地和食物。

sentences.en: The history of agriculture has been a history of control.
sentences.zh: 农业史一直是一部控制史。

sentences.en: Trying to bend nature to our will and make it predictable and productive.
sentences.zh: 试图让自然顺从我们的意愿，使其变得可预测且富有成效。

sentences.en: But for the sake of the bees, and maybe even for the future of our food supply,
sentences.zh: 但为了蜜蜂的福祉，或许也为了我们食物供应的未来，

sentences.en: we might need an agricultural system that's just a little bit more wild.
sentences.zh: 我们需要一个更加野性一点的农业系统。

sentences.en: More with Adam about how domesticated bees became a symbol of conservation.
sentences.zh: 接下来将与亚当探讨家养蜜蜂是如何成为保护象征的更多内容。

sentences.en: After this.
sentences.zh: 广告之后见。

sentences.en: So in the story, you mentioned that Save the Bees has become a big part of the conservation movement in the last couple of years.
sentences.zh: 所以在故事中，你提到“拯救蜜蜂”在过去几年里成为了保护运动的重要组成部分。

sentences.en: And when I was a kid, it was all, you know, whales and pandas and other charismatic megafauna.
sentences.zh: 当我还是个孩子的时候，你知道的，全都是鲸鱼、大熊猫和其他有魅力的巨型动物。

sentences.en: And how did bees take off as both a focus of activism and as a symbol?
sentences.zh: 蜜蜂是如何作为一个行动主义焦点和一个象征腾飞的呢？

sentences.en: Well, I think it really started around 2006 with the, you know, with the onset of the colony collapse disorder scare.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为它确实始于2006年前后，随着蜂群崩溃综合征恐慌的爆发。

sentences.en: Honeybees really became this symbol of confluence of all these environmental probleMs.
sentences.zh: 蜜蜂真正成为了所有这些环境问题交汇的象征。

sentences.en: And they had the advantage of being cute and cuddly and easily identifiable creatures, you know.
sentences.zh: 而且它们具有可爱、呆萌且易于识别的生物优势，你知道的。

sentences.en: So environmentalists really latched on to them.
sentences.zh: 所以环保主义者真的紧紧抓住了它们。

sentences.en: And in some cases, some states actually sued to create protections for honeybees.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，一些州甚至起诉以建立对蜜蜂的保护措施。

sentences.en: You know, you probably heard the protests.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你可能听说过那些抗议活动。

sentences.en: There was actually a really huge protest in the UK a few years back where protesters dressed up like Winnie the Pooh were holding signs and, you know, singing songs.
sentences.zh: 几年前英国实际上有一场非常大型的抗议活动，抗议者们扮成小熊维尼的模样，举着标语，唱着歌。

sentences.en: And basically, we are all beekeepers.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是，我们都是养蜂人。

sentences.en: Winnie the Pooh wasn't the greatest beekeeper.
sentences.zh: 小熊维尼并不是最棒的养蜂人。

sentences.en: No, and in fact, yeah, you know, most of those hives that Winnie the Pooh was actually robbing were paper wasps, which don't actually produce honey.
sentences.zh: 是的，而且事实上，你知道的，小熊维尼实际上去掏的那些蜂巢大部分都是黄胡蜂的，它们实际上不产蜂蜜。

sentences.en: But so when you talk to most people about saving the bees, the image that they probably have in their head is like of an orange and black honeybee.
sentences.zh: 所以当你和大多数人谈论拯救蜜蜂时，他们脑海中浮现的形象可能就像是一只橙黑相间的蜜蜂。

sentences.en: And this is the result of all of this promotion and cartoon bees, like the Honey Nut Cheerios bee.
sentences.zh: 这是所有这些宣传和卡通蜜蜂（比如乐家坚果蜂蜜麦圈的蜜蜂）共同作用的结果。

sentences.en: One person I spoke with for this series, Catherine Baldock, she's a biologist in the UK.
sentences.zh: 我为这个系列采访过的一个人，凯瑟琳·鲍多克，她是英国的一位生物学家。

sentences.en: And she says the big reason people care about bees and conservation is the honeybee.
sentences.zh: 她说人们关心蜜蜂和保护工作的主要原因就是蜜蜂。

sentences.en: They're kind of like the panda, aren't they, of invertebrate conservation.
sentences.zh: 它们有点像无脊椎动物保护中的大熊猫，不是吗？

sentences.en: I think it is a good thing by conserving or by trying to help bees with generally improving habitats, putting more flowers in.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一件好事，通过保护或试图通过普遍改善栖息地、种植更多花卉来帮助蜜蜂。

sentences.en: And that's going to benefit a whole host of other kind of species.
sentences.zh: 这将造福一大批其他种类的物种。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I think it's a good thing.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我认为这是一件好事。

sentences.en: They're kind of like a bit of a symbol of conservation in a way, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，它们有点像保护的象征，不是吗？

sentences.en: The panda of bees are struggling.
sentences.zh: 大熊猫蜜蜂正处于挣扎之中。

sentences.en: In fact, we're losing about 40 percent per year, but they aren't an extinction risk.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们每年损失约百分之四十，但它们没有灭绝的风险。

sentences.en: You know, they're managed just like cows or sheep.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，它们就像牛或羊一样被管理着。

sentences.en: So they'll probably be OK.
sentences.zh: 所以它们可能会没事的。

sentences.en: It's really the native bees that we're worried about.
sentences.zh: 我们真正担心的是本地蜜蜂。

sentences.en: And the key distinction here is that things that benefit honeybees don't always benefit native bees,
sentences.zh: 这里的一个关键区别是，对蜜蜂有益的事情并不总是对本地蜜蜂有益，

sentences.en: especially when the two species are competing for the same resources, you know.
sentences.zh: 特别是当这两个物种在争夺相同的资源时，你知道的。

sentences.en: So actually, this has kind of become a problem in recent years.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，这在近年来已经成为一个问题。

sentences.en: Beekeepers have lobbied the federal government to be allowed to put their honeybee hives into national parks,
sentences.zh: 养蜂人游说联邦政府允许他们将蜂箱放入国家公园，

sentences.en: where the bees then can outcompete native bees for the floral resources.
sentences.zh: 蜜蜂在那里会为了花卉资源而在竞争中胜过本地蜜蜂。

sentences.en: So that's a case where you have this managed species, a honeybee, outcompeting with a native species.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是一个被管理的物种——蜜蜂，在竞争中胜过本地物种的例子。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So honeybees might not be a great symbol for conservation after all.
sentences.zh: 所以蜜蜂可能终究不是一个很好的保护象征。

sentences.en: So what species would be more accurate if you wanted to have an invertebrate mascot for environmentalists?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果你想为环保主义者找一个无脊椎动物吉祥物，什么物种会更准确呢？

sentences.en: Well, there's no shortage of candidates, that's for sure.
sentences.zh: 嗯，候选者绝对不缺。

sentences.en: You know, about 20,000 bee species in the world.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，世界上大约有20,000种蜜蜂。

sentences.en: But, you know, let's run through just a couple that spring to the top of your mind.
sentences.zh: 不过，你知道的，我们不妨快速列举几个你脑海中最先蹦出来的例子。

sentences.en: The black sweat bee, you know, this is kind of like the Ozzy Osbourne of bees, you know, all black.
sentences.zh: 黑汗蜂，你知道的，这有点像是蜜蜂里的奥兹·奥斯本，通体全黑。

sentences.en: Kind of looks more like a fly with these kind of purple eyes.
sentences.zh: 它看起来更像是一只苍蝇，长着这种紫色的眼睛。

sentences.en: You know, you've got ground nesting bees like the mason bees, which are, you know, kind of resemble honeybees.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你还会看到像壁蜂这样的地栖蜂，它们，你知道的，有点像蜜蜂。

sentences.en: A little more shaggy, a little more rough around the edges.
sentences.zh: 毛发更蓬乱一些，外表更粗犷一些。

sentences.en: And then the rusty patched bumblebee, which was actually recently added to the endangered species list, is actually quite cute and cuddly.
sentences.zh: 而锈斑大黄蜂，最近刚刚被列入濒危物种名单，其实长得相当可爱且招人喜欢。

sentences.en: You know, it looks like a bumblebee, except it's got these two little rust-colored orange patches on its back.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，它看起来就像一只大黄蜂，只不过背上有两个橘红色的锈色斑块。

sentences.en: That would be a bee that could compete, you know, on cuteness alone.
sentences.zh: 单凭可爱程度，这也是一种能有一拼的蜜蜂。

sentences.en: Other than finding the perfect fuzzy symbol for conservation when it comes to bees, if people are concerned about bees and the health of bee populations, what can they do?
sentences.zh: 除了为蜜蜂寻找完美的毛茸茸的自然保护象征之外，如果人们关心蜜蜂和蜂群的健康，他们能做些什么呢？

sentences.en: Well, you know, this is where there's a bit of good news, because unlike other big looming environmental issues,
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道的，这里有个好消息，因为不像其他那些迫在眉睫的宏大环境问题——

sentences.en: which can kind of be abstract or maybe difficult to wrap your head around in terms of individual action.
sentences.zh: 那些问题可能有点抽象，或者就个人行动而言可能很难让人理解。

sentences.en: You know, things like climate change, for instance, with pollinators, you can actually do something that will create direct benefit for bees.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，比如气候变化之类的事情，但对于传粉昆虫，你其实可以做一些能为蜜蜂带来直接益处的事。

sentences.en: This doesn't include, you know, unfortunately, buying things like local honey from the farmer's market.
sentences.zh: 这并不包括，你知道的，不幸的是，去农夫市场上买当地产的蜂蜜之类的事情。

sentences.en: And don't get me wrong, I love honey, but it doesn't actually help native bees if we're purchasing a product that's created by honeybees.
sentences.zh: 别误会我的意思，我喜欢蜂蜜，但如果我们购买的是由蜜蜂生产的产品，这其实对本地蜂毫无帮助。

sentences.en: The same thing goes with backyard beekeeping.
sentences.zh: 后院养蜂也是同样的道理。

sentences.en: It doesn't do anything to help pollinators by raising basically this agricultural livestock.
sentences.zh: 饲养这种基本上属于农业家畜的动物，对帮助传粉昆虫毫无用处。

sentences.en: You know, so toward that end, there are things you can do, which is obviously plant more native flowers and plants in your yard.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，所以为了达到这个目的，你可以做一些事情，显然就是在你的院子里种更多的本土花卉和植物。

sentences.en: Plants that can bloom at different times throughout the year to give those bees something to feed on.
sentences.zh: 这些植物可以在一年中的不同时间开花，给那些蜜蜂提供食物。

sentences.en: Other things, obviously, like avoiding pesticides, for example, you know, or perhaps consider letting your lawn go a bit wild,
sentences.zh: 当然，其他事情还包括避免使用杀虫剂，例如，你知道的，或者可以考虑让你的草坪稍微荒野一点，

sentences.en: letting all those dandelions come up in the springtime.
sentences.zh: 让那些蒲公英在春天全部长出来。

sentences.en: Those are things that can really help native pollinators quite a bit.
sentences.zh: 这些都是能对本土传粉昆虫起到很大帮助的事情。

sentences.en: I'm so excited about this because I hate taking care of the lawn and letting it go wild is exactly in keeping with both my ethic as a conservationist and as a lazy human.
sentences.zh: 我对此感到非常兴奋，因为我讨厌打理草坪，而让它野蛮生长完全符合我作为环保主义者和懒惰人类的双重道德标准。

sentences.en: It seems perfect for me.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说简直完美。

sentences.en: There you go.
sentences.zh: 这就对了。

sentences.en: Now you've got an explanation.
sentences.zh: 现在你有了借口。

sentences.en: Because the neighbors get mad and I can just say I'm doing it for the bees.
sentences.zh: 因为邻居们会生气的，而我可以说我这么做是为了蜜蜂。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thank you, Roman.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，罗曼。

sentences.en: If you'd like to hear more about the connections between honeybees and our environmental landscape, you should check out Adam's show.
sentences.zh: 如果你想了解更多关于蜜蜂与我们生态环境之间联系的信息，你应该去听听亚当的节目。

sentences.en: It's called The Business of Bees.
sentences.zh: 节目名叫《蜜蜂的生意》。

sentences.en: It's available everywhere you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 各大播客平台均可收听。

sentences.zh: 本周的《99%无形》由亚当·阿灵顿制作，克里斯·贝鲁布剪辑，谢里夫·优素福负责混音和技术制作，肖恩·里亚尔配乐。

sentences.zh: 凯蒂·明格是我们资深制作人。

sentences.zh: 库尔特·科尔斯塔德是数字总监。

sentences.en: The rest of the team is Emmett Fitzgerald, Avery Troubleman, Joe Rosenberg, Vivian Lee, Delaney Hall, Sophia Klatzker, and me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 团队其他成员包括埃梅特·菲茨杰拉德、艾弗里·特鲁布曼、乔·罗森伯格、维维安·李、德兰尼·霍尔、索菲亚·克拉茨克，以及我，罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.zh: 我们是旧金山 91.7 KALW 的一个项目，制作地点位于加利福尼亚州奥克兰市中心美丽的广播街。

sentences.zh: 《99%无形》是 PRX 旗下 Radiotopia 的成员，这是一个由播客界最具创新性的节目组成的坚定的独立联盟。

sentences.zh: 请访问 radiotopia.fm 了解全部节目。

sentences.zh: 你可以发推特@我（@Roman Mars）以及节目（@99pi.org）。

sentences.zh: 我们也在 Instagram 和 Reddit 上。

sentences.zh: 不过，随时欢迎你来我们位于 99pi.org 的大本营做客。
